notes.title: Demo 0.8.21 Update — Lots of New Cards & QoL Improvements
notes.content:
It’s been a while since I last wrote an update log—I’ve quietly pushed some changes behind the scenes.
But that’s not really fair to everyone, so here we go.
[hr][/hr]🧟 Fracture
A large batch of new cards has been added. Some still don’t have their final artwork yet, but I wanted to let everyone try them out.

Many of these cards focus on synergy and combo mechanics, which should help address some of the clunky feedback players gave before.

Some of the new interactions might even feel a bit overpowered… but hey, let’s see what happens once players break the game.
[hr][/hr]🩸 Sanguinar
The Ranger also received some new cards, and a few old ones were removed.

The new cards mostly revolve around the evasion mechanic. For example:

Shadowstep doubles your Evasion.

Afterimage restores lost Evasion.

The focus here is on dynamics. While stacking defense endlessly is fun and relaxing, I wanted players to experience a constant ebb and flow—like a rollercoaster.

Evasion is Sanguinar’s signature defensive tool, and these cards are designed to reflect that.

Also, if you noticed, a few Sanguinar's cards were “borrowed” by Fracture… (they supposedly volunteered).
[hr][/hr]✨ QoL Improvements
Numeric hotkeys now let you select cards quickly.

Quick-play support: cards will queue and resolve automatically after being played.

Hovering over a card gradually shows its keyword explanations.

Clicking on a Splitter on the field lets you inspect its feeding pile.

notes.title: Demo 0.8.1 Update — A Wave of Balance Changes & QoL Improvements
notes.content:
⚔️ Evasion Mechanic Rework
The previous Evasion system had some depth, but the concept of Agility often caused confusion.
This time I’ve reworked evasion once again, making it easier to understand while keeping its unique depth:

Evasion:
When attacked, reduce final damage by the number of Evasion stacks, then halve the Evasion stacks.
[hr][/hr]🃏 Evasion-Related Card Reworks
Roll and Evade: Discard 1 card, gain 8 Evasion.

Daring Step: Gain 6 Evasion. If you lose HP from an attack this turn, lose all Dodge.

Spinback: Gain the amount of Evasion you have previously lost this battle. Shuffle. Deplete.

Shadow Cloak: Gain 4 Evasion whenever attacked.

Scarlet Phantom: Gain 2 Evasion whenever you gain Bleed.

Phantom Sword: Deal damage equal to Evasion stacks, then halve Evasion stacks. Repeat until all Evasion is gone. Then restore all Evasion.
[hr][/hr]🩸 Blood Ranger Card Adjustments
Cleave: Now has Instant.

Incurable Curse: Target’s Bleed will never decrease (until battle ends). Now has Deplete.

Bloodburst: Becomes 0-cost when upgraded.

Crimson Thorn: Duration 3 → 5.

Scab: Healing 5 → 8.

Pierce the Heart: Damage 12 → 16, Bleed 12 → 16.
[hr][/hr]🧟 Flesh Aberration Card Adjustments
Red Eyes → Show-off: Deal 2 attack damage. For each other creature on the field, attack 1 additional time.

Big Mouth: Now increases number of attacks when fed.

Peacekeeper: Gains 99 Taunt when summoned.

Meat Mountain: Taunt intent removed.

Sapling: HP growth per turn 5 → 10.

Locked Target: Cost 1 → 0, now has Exhaust.

Grimace Assault: Damage 10 → 14.

Slide Tackle: Damage 7 → 8.

Feast: Cost 3(2) → 2(1).

Flesh Bomb: Cost 2 → 1.

Beast Stance: Strength 3 → 4.

Berserk: Negative effect changed to -3 max temporary HP.

Stand Forward: Taunt 2(3) → 4(6).
[hr][/hr]🛡️ Taunt & Multi-Hit Attack Interaction
Attacks targeting random enemies are now also affected by Taunt.

Multi-hit attacks from monsters and splitters are now treated as random attacks.

Example: The Castle Archer’s “Multi-Shot 4×6” will no longer keep shooting a dead splitter, but instead redirect to the next target.

On the flip side, when your splitter uses “5×8,” it won’t waste all hits on a single enemy, but will spread them across all enemies.
[hr][/hr]🕯️ Other Adjustments
Foul Cards: Can no longer be drawn actively, but 1 is automatically drawn at the start of each turn.

Parasite Adjustments:

Bone Sprout: Negative effect changed to -3(2) max HP after each battle.

Clumsy Toe: Negative effect changed to -1(2) max hand size.
[hr][/hr]✨ QoL Improvements
All buff icons have been redrawn, finally ending the era of identical placeholder icons stacked together.

Buff icons now appear next to buff names in descriptions, showing their stacks.

During your turn, playable cards glow. If playing one would increase Sin, they glow black instead.
[hr][/hr]🐞 Bug Fixes
Fixed Revenge still resetting cost when played under Murderous Resolve (was this even a bug?).

Fixed monsters’ minions still acting after their leader was killed.

Fixed some cards freezing when discarding those with the Instant keyword.

notes.title: Demo 0.8.0 Patch Notes — New Class! The Fracture Arrives!
notes.content:
🌟 New Class: Fracture
The initial version of Fracture is here!

Currently, he comes with 45 cards. While the number isn’t huge, it’s already enough to test his core mechanics. (In fact, I still have many ideas that didn’t make it in yet!)

Balancing such a unique mechanic as the Splitters is an extraordinary challenge, so I’ll be keeping a close eye on feedback and making adjustments as needed.

I can’t wait to see what players think — if you have any feedback, please feel free to reach out!



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45325967/5a58dfc54db16a05b352d3e695f447656e8cd177.png"]


[hr][/hr]🩸 Sanguinar’s Starting Deck Adjustment
Previously, the Sanguinar’s starting deck was too bland — not only unfun to play, but it also failed to highlight his unique traits.

So, I broke away from the principle of “starting decks should remain simple” and remade 2 of his starting cards:

Stab → Bloodarrow

Cost: 1

Deal 4 attack damage.

Consume all your Bleed, applying the same amount of Armor Break to the target.

Minor Heal → Bloodheal

Cost: 1

Heal 6 Wounded HP.

Gain 2 Bleed.

Instant. (When this card is discarded, it is automatically played without consuming Power.)


[hr][/hr]📖 Terminology Update
There are actually two types of healing in the game:

One restores only Wounded HP,

The other restores HP directly.

Previously, these two effects were easy to confuse. From now on, they will use different terms:

Restoring damaged HP will be referred to as “Heal.”

Restoring HP directly will be referred to as “Recover.”

notes.title: ✨ Demo v0.7.7 Update —— Resolve Level
notes.content:
New Hero Progression System — Resolve Level Unlocked!



🧠 Earn Echoes to Unlock Cards

At the end of each run, the Echoes of Memory you collect will now also contribute to increasing the Resolve Level of the hero you played.



🔓 Leveling up Resolve unlocks new cards for that hero.

We’ve chosen to lock certain cards early on — not to restrict player freedom, but to offer gentle progression and onboarding.

Some cards are more complex or situational, and may be difficult to utilize early on.
As you level up, you’ll unlock cards with internal synergies and theme-based mechanics,
encouraging you to explore new builds and playstyles.

notes.title: Demo v0.7.0 Update — A Radical Attempt
notes.content:
Welcome back!
This update introduces a bold gameplay change: a complete rework of the card draw system.


[hr][/hr]

🔄 A Brand-New Draw Mechanic
The draw pile is now divided into 4 separate piles based on card types:

Ritual

Attack

Skill

Ability

Whenever you draw a card, you can freely choose which pile to draw from, one card at a time.
If a pile runs empty, a reshuffle button will appear below it — though reshuffling costs 1 draw.

This seemingly simple change brings a whole new layer of strategy and experience.


Players now have far more control over how their turns unfold. 

In fact, it feels like the system forces you to think and make intentional decisions.

During internal testing, I found myself constantly evaluating the situation before every draw — building a sense of anticipation.

And as the draw progresses, that anticipation is either fulfilled… or not.



Of course, the system isn’t without risk:

The learning curve is definitely steeper, and new players may struggle to understand when to draw from which pile.

And in long runs, constantly choosing which pile to draw from might become a bit tiring.

But these are just my predictions.
Your real feedback will be invaluable in helping me improve this system going forward.


[hr][/hr]

🛠️ Card Changes (to fit the new draw system)
Drawblade

Old: Keep drawing until an Attack is found, discarding all non-Attack cards

New: Draw 1 card from the Attack pile. That card costs -1 this turn. Exhaust.

Block Perception

Old: Discard up to 3 cards from the top of the draw pile; heal 5 for each

New: Discard exactly 2 cards from the top of the draw pile; heal 7 for each

⚠️ Some cards are temporarily disabled because they don’t work well with the new system:

Hide the Price

Twist Fate


[hr][/hr]

☠️ Changes to Curse and Torment Cards
When gained during combat, Curses and Torment cards will now be placed on top of a random draw pile

The effect “gaining Taint when retained” has been removed

So now, you’re free to play, keep, or discard them — entirely your call.


[hr][/hr]


That’s everything for this update.
I truly hope you enjoy the new draw system. If anything feels confusing, annoying, or just not right — please do leave your feedback, either here or in-game!

—

If you like the update — or just like the game —
a wishlist, review, or recommending it to a friend would mean the world to me. ❤️

notes.title: Demo v0.6.9 Update Notes
notes.content:
🃏 Curse & Torment Keyword Adjustments

Removed the Stubborn keyword from all Curse and Torment cards

Added Cycle or Proliferate instead

Without “Stubborn,” these cards can now be discarded freely when overdrawn —
though their price may now be more subtly hidden...

🌙 Multiple Foul Cards per Night

You can now obtain multiple Foul cards in a single night

As long as you have enough Tainted Desire, you can keep drawing them

⚔️ Card Adjustment: Sword Drawing

When the draw pile is empty, it now reshuffles and continues drawing until an Attack is found

If no Attack card exists in both draw and discard piles, the card becomes unusable

🧠 Hand Limit Adjustment

Maximum hand size reverted from 9 to 7

🐛 Bug Fixes

Fixed incorrect power cost and damage display for Crazy Slash

Fixed Coagulated Spike being playable without any Bleed

Fixed soft lock when retaining a Curse that triggers Torment at turn end

notes.title: Divine Sin Demo is Now Live — Try It Now!
notes.content:
A Word from the Developer

One year ago, a fool gave up a well-paid job to start making this game alone.
Day after day, he poured a part of his soul into the project.
In the countless moments of pain and joy, there were so many things he wanted to say.
But now, at the very moment the demo is finally released, he finds that no words can truly capture this overwhelming feeling.

So, with that said—
Hope you have fun playing.


🎮 Demo Content


 1 playable hero
 100+ cards
 3 major stage zones (including 40 regular enemies, 6 elites, and 3 bosses)


The full version will contain roughly 3 to 4 times more content.


v0.6.1 Update Notes (compared to v0.5.5)

🎨 Card Art Redraw

 All of the Sanguinar’s cards (except for ritual cards) now have official artwork.


🧭 Tutorial Added

A basic rules tutorial has been added. If the game still feels difficult to pick up, feel free to leave feedback!


🃏 Card Balance Adjustments

No Regrets

 Heal 1(2) → Heal 2(3)

Phantom Clone

 Now includes Deplete
 Upgrade no longer reduces cost, but removes Deplete

Blood for Blood

 Cost 2 → 1
 Now includes Deplete
 Upgrade no longer reduces cost, but removes Deplete

Crazy Slash

 Damage 7~14 (10~20) → 7~9 (10~12)

Harvest+

 Apply 8 Bleeding → Apply 6 Bleeding 


Blood Echo

 Card type changed from Skill → Ability


Quick Slash+

 Upgrade no longer increases draw, now increases damage
 Damage 8~10, Draw 2 → Damage 12~14, Draw 1


🐞 Known Bugs

 The boss Giant King in Area 3 sometimes incorrectly gains attack power every time it takes damage. Cause unknown.
 Switching languages repeatedly may cause text display issues. Restarting the game will fix it.

Apologies to players who encounter any bugs.
If you discover new ones, you're welcome to report them directly in-game.
